subject: Post-demo: security qualification recap, SOC 2 Type II ask & TrustLocker provisioning
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orthoworks.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@orthoworks.com>, procure@orthoworks.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: security qualification recap, SOC 2 Type II ask & TrustLocker provisioning

Hi Liam / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the security/compliance front so your security team can move forward: 

1) SOC 2 status: we have a SOC 2 Type II report for 2027 (covering relevant controls). I can share a summary and a redacted report snapshot.
2) Temporary attestation / bridge letter: we can provide a bridge letter (temp attestation) while the full artifact is shared with your security portal.
3) Portal access: we use TrustLocker for secure evidence exchange — I can invite your security contact to onboard and drop artifacts.
4) VSQ (vendor security questionnaire): happy to kick off the questionnaire — attached is our standard vendor security questionnaire (xlsx) and a one-page SOC 2 summary.

Ask: Can you confirm the right security contact (is it Olivia?) and whether OrthoWorks needs HIPAA-specific language or EU data residency notes for this engagement? Also let me know if procurement needs a PO template before we ship the bridge letter.

I attached: vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (stub), SOC2_TypeII_2027-summary.pdf (stub). I will also prepare a bridge_letter PDF and share via TrustLocker link once I have the contact email.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm security contact + any jurisdictional requirements (HIPAA/GDPR)
- Us: send TrustLocker invite + bridge letter + redacted SOC2 snapshot
- Both: schedule a 30-min security intake if your team wants a walkthrough

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), SOC2_TypeII_2027-summary.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orthoworks.com>

Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@orthoworks.com>, procure@orthoworks.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 09:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security qualification recap, SOC 2 Type II ask & TrustLocker provisioning

Kimberly —

Appreciate the follow-up and the materials. A few clarifying items from our security and procurement teams: 

- Confirm the SOC 2 Type II report date range (we need coverage into Q3 2027). Is the report full Type II (period-based) or a summary?
- HIPAA: yes — we'll be processing limited PHI for scheduling workflows. We need assurance on BAAs and controls around encryption at rest (KMS) and access logging.
- Data residency: OrthoWorks will keep patient data in the US; please confirm host regions and whether any EU data processing happens.
- Bridge letter: procurement wants a dated bridge letter they can attach to our vendor record while they wait for the full report. Do you have a template?

Also, can you provision TrustLocker access for olivia.park@orthoworks.com and procure@orthoworks.com? If we proceed, procurement will probably request a quote and a PO.

Thanks —
Liam
Senior Product Manager, OrthoWorks
liam.oconnor@orthoworks.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: security qualification recap, SOC 2 Type II ask & TrustLocker provisioning

Liam —

Thanks — answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

- SOC 2 scope/date: the 2027 SOC 2 Type II is a full period report (Jan 1 2027 - Dec 31 2027). I attached a one-page summary; if you need a redacted copy we can upload it to TrustLocker.
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports BAAs for customers handling PHI. Our controls include AES-256 at rest with KMS integration, TLS 1.2+ in transit, and detailed access logging. We can provide our HIPAA control mapping in the VSQ.
- Data residency: Hosted regions are US (primary), with optional eu-west for EU-only residency — no EU processing will occur by default for US-region tenants. I will confirm the deployment region we would use for your account in the onboarding doc.
- Bridge letter: yes — we have a dated temporary attestation (bridge letter) template. I'm attaching the bridge letter PDF now and will also drop it into TrustLocker.

TrustLocker invite: I just provisioned invites to the following addresses: olivia.park@orthoworks.com, procure@orthoworks.com. Expect an invite email from TrustLocker (support@trustlocker.example) with onboarding instructions — please check spam if you don't see it in 10-15 minutes.

Proposed next steps:
- We: upload redacted SOC2 snapshot + bridge_letter_temp_attestation.pdf to TrustLocker (done)
- OrthoWorks: confirm receipt and any redaction needs
- Both: schedule 30-min security intake (I propose Wed 7/3 11:00am PDT)

I attached bridge letter: redwood_bridge_letter_temp_attestation.pdf (stub). Aditya — tagging you on timeline for a copy of the full report handoff and any SFTP fallback options if TrustLocker proves slow for large artifacts.

Thanks —
Kimberly

Attachments: redwood_bridge_letter_temp_attestation.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orthoworks.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security qualification recap, SOC 2 Type II ask & TrustLocker provisioning

Looping in time/control notes —

Liam / Olivia — quick operational notes from our infra/compliance side: 
- SOC 2 full report: we can provide redacted Type II artifacts immediately via TrustLocker. The unredacted report requires an NDA/PO in some enterprise cases; we'll coordinate with procurement.
- Timeline: once TrustLocker access is accepted we typically complete the evidence handoff within 24-48 hours for redacted items; full report coordination can take up to 7 business days depending on the approval flow.
- SFTP fallback: if TrustLocker upload is blocked by your IT, we can use an SFTP drop with time-limited credentials; will set this up on request.
- BAA: our legal team has a standard BAA; procurement can request the template and we can fast-track review.

I'll include the hubspot deal (linked) and I'll attach the signed bridge-letter template for procurement to upload — see related links.

Aditya Rao
Director, Infrastructure & Compliance, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
